scope.unit: complete materialized publishable view; independent random 32-byte read key per view and epoch
scope.authorization: a read-key holder can decrypt every entry in that view; target selection is not per-key cryptographic ACL
scope.readers: machines get read key only, never a publisher private key
scope.publishers: separate random Ed25519 signing authority; distinct read and publish password wrapping domains. Possession of publish key is publication authority; shared key does not provide per-user attribution or threshold approval
scope.compromisedClient: trusted independently distributed writer client required; malicious JavaScript from a compromised panel can use unlocked keys

algorithms.canonicalization: RFC8785 JCS restricted fixed-ASCII-property schema; UTF-8 without BOM; no duplicate/unknown properties, floats, NaN, unpaired surrogates; counters decimal strings (uint64). Metadata paths/names NFC canonical; values unchanged exact Unicode scalar sequences.
algorithms.counterRules: uint64 canonical decimal 0..18446744073709551615; no leading zero; sequences start at1; epoch>=1; overflow stops publication
algorithms.encodings: UUID lowercase canonical; hashes lowercase hex64; binary fields canonical unpadded Base64url, exact decoded lengths checked
algorithms.entryOrdering: strict increasing UTF-8 tuple(path,name); duplicate tuples forbidden; paths canonical segment-aware POSIX; reject rather than silently normalize
algorithms.parentOrdering: parent refs ordered by UTF-8 UUID tuple; duplicate source contexts forbidden, even with different sequence/hash
algorithms.metadata: paths and names must be NFC; reject Unicode categories Cc,Cf,Cs including DEL/C1/bidi/zero-width; values are unchanged Unicode scalar strings

envelope.plaintext: complete context + complete ordered entries array. Names/paths/values are jointly authenticated inside whole ciphertext. entry_count must match.
envelope.nonces: fresh CSPRNG salt32 and nonce12 for every new encryption attempt, including CAS rebase. Retrying identical already-staged immutable envelope is idempotent and reuses exact bytes.
envelope.noPlaintextDigests: never publish hashes of plaintext/low-entropy values. Envelope hashes cover randomized ciphertext.
envelope.initial: sequence1 previous_hash=64 zeroes; registration genesis seq0/hash0 is not a consumable snapshot
envelope.restore: explicit user-authorized restore is a NEW sequence with fresh encryption, action=restore, restored_from=old envelopeHash; never moves head backward

readKeyWrap.format: new e2e2 wrapper endpoint, no e2e1 auto-fallback
readKeyWrap.context: protocol + realm/project/environment/view/log UUIDs + readKeyEpoch + publisherPolicyEpoch + recipient fingerprint
readKeyWrap.payload: only viewReadKey32 and exact bound context; no project-wide master key or publisher private key
readKeyWrap.payloadWire: JCS({format:'sekvyr-e2e2-read-key-v1',context:exact signed WrapContext,read_key:canonical unpadded Base64url of32 bytes}); exact fields only; plaintext <=2048 bytes, ciphertext <=2064 bytes; no publisher private material
readKeyWrap.p256Encoding: uncompressed SEC1 public point, exactly65 bytes; recipient_fingerprint='p256-sha256:'+lowercase hex SHA256 of these65 bytes. Existing node key is supplied as one unencrypted PKCS8 PEM P-256 key and is never generated or replaced by the reader.
readKeyWrap.signature: Ed25519.Sign(publisherKey, UTF8('sekvyr-e2e2/reader-wrap-sign/v1')||0x00||JCS(body)); publisher policy and epoch must be independently trusted
readKeyWrap.verification: verify allowed publisher signature/policy, recipient, UUIDs and current read-key epoch before unwrapping; AEAD context must match signed canonical snapshot
readKeyWrap.rotation: new node key requires new wrappers, not automatic trust reset. Revoking a view reader requires fresh read-key epoch and wrappers for remaining readers; old disclosed data cannot be recalled.
readKeyWrap.memory: unwrapped view key lives in memory only; no raw view key or publish secret in CR/status/logs/temp files

publication.authoritativeCommit: successful conditional append to canonical witness ledger; panel current pointer is derived only
steps: fetch fresh witness head and verify canonical base by hash
decrypt trusted base and apply explicit reviewed diff; never reconstruct from unsigned server fields
approver unlocks publisher key, verifies full final view and re-encrypts/signs
stage immutable envelope under computed hash in panel
witness checks downloadable staged exact hash, publisher signature and registered source/policy
witness atomically CAS-appends seq=head+1,prev=headHash,newHash to durable independent ledger
panel indexes committed head; interrupted indexing is recovered by exact hash
publication.conflicts: only one successor per canonical head. Conflict requires refetch, visible diff and explicit new confirmation; no automatic semantic rebase/signing
publication.crashAfterCommit: witness-committed hash remains canonical if panel pointer update fails. Fetch by hash is mandatory. Missing bytes -> CanonicalSnapshotUnavailable; no older-head fallback.
publication.proposals: separate intent/domain; proposals and pending versions are never published snapshots. Final approver signs complete snapshot after approval. Legacy approve_version cannot publish e2e2.
publication.businessCompleteness: signature proves completeness of publisher-approved set, not truth of unsigned source. Trusted base must come from witness.
publication.multiView: CAS is per-view. No atomic cross-view publication in first profile; edits/revocation/parent propagation require explicit publication of every affected view.

witness.component: one logical independent checkpoint-witness, not panel and not an operator-local mutable checkpoint. HA uses verified linearizable storage, no custom quorum protocol.
witness.trust: witness verify key,epoch,logID,initial min checkpoint and allowed publisher policy provisioned independently; never learned solely from panel
witness.headAPI: POST /v1/logs/{log_id}/head-challenge with fresh 32-byte request_nonce; signed response uses sekvyr-e2e2/head/v1 domain over JCS(body), exact schema
witness.readPrivacy: head API exposes only opaque identifiers, revisions and ciphertext-derived hashes; no secret values, names or AES keys. Read checkpoints are public metadata; TLS, rate limits and optional network restriction apply.
witness.commitAPI: POST /v1/logs/{log_id}/commits expected=(witnessEpoch,seq,hash,policyEpoch), new envelopeHash; validates staged envelope against fixed registered origin, no arbitrary fetch URL or redirects
witness.ledger: independent non-overwritable append-only canonical journal with linearizable ReadHead and conditional AppendIfHead, unique sequence and previous hash. Cache/SQL index is derivative, not authority.
witness.durability: ledger append must be durably acknowledged before commit receipt or fresh head response. Signing/cache cannot get ahead of ledger. ReadHead must not use stale replica/cache.
witness.restore: rebuild witness state from external canonical journal; never restore canonical head solely from panel/operator backups. If journal consistency/freshness cannot be established, witness not ready and cannot sign fresh head.
witness.externalAnchorRequirement: storage adapter must prove immutability/conditional append, durable monotonic reads and independence from panel/operator restores. An ordinary periodically backed-up database alone does not satisfy this profile.
witness.rootBoundary: if witness keys plus ALL canonical journal/independent checkpoints are compromised or rolled back together, protocol cannot detect the lost history. No infinite witness chain or absolute all-roots-rollback promise.
witness.administrativeAPI: log registration, writer/witness policy changes and log reset require independent administrative authority; panel credential alone cannot register or reset trust
witness.noAvailabilityGuarantee: withholding/disappearing staged ciphertext can cause denial of service even after commit; cannot forge a canonical old head
witness.floorProof: head request includes trusted floor=(seq,hash); ledger validates that exact canonical historical record and signs verified floor in fresh head proof. Higher head alone is not proof that an arbitrary pinned older hash was canonical.
witness.ledgerAuthority: canonical journal includes root log registration/genesis and ALL authority transitions: publisher keysets and policy activations/revocations, read-key epochs, witness key/epoch transitions and administrative recovery. Authorization state is derived from verified journal, never restored cache/config alone.
witness.transitions: administrative events need pinned independent recovery/admin authority signatures and conditional append. Policy activation plus canonical new snapshot is one ledger transition; head-only rebuild cannot resurrect a revoked signer.
witness.crossRules: head seq/hash/readKeyEpoch/policyEpoch must equal chosen envelope; no epoch0 for seq>0, uint64 bounds apply to proof/floor; ledger forbids epoch decrease and enforces registered allowed policy/read-key transitions
witness.trustAssumption: WitnessCurrent assumes an honest independently administered witness plus authentic linearizable ledger and uncompromised verification/signing trust. A malicious witness with valid signing authority may lie about freshness to a new/restored reader even without rolling back the journal. Single witness is not Byzantine tolerance.

reader.bootstrap: independent signed/admin trust bundle binds IDs, node key, publisher policy, witness key/epoch/logID and minimum seq/hash checkpoint. Genesis not TOFU.
steps: request fresh signed witness head with nonce and trusted floor=max(bootstrap checkpoint,local high-watermark); verify signed exact floor and all identifiers
reject below local high-watermark, same seq/different hash or mismatched trust/policy/epoch
fetch exact canonical hash; validate schema,JCS limits,signature,context and wrapping key
decrypt entire view and validate complete canonical entries and count
request second fresh nonce head using first head as verified floor; if advanced discard candidate and retry at most3 times
durably persist accepted checkpoint before target mutation
derive selected deterministic target bytes; atomically persist data+opaque revision+accepted checkpoint+eligible rollout intent only if bytes changed
report sanitized status; never label witness failure or older target as current
reader.commitRace: latest at the second linearizable witness check, not guaranteed latest at subsequent Kubernetes write or forever; later commits converge by polling
reader.checkpoint: namespace/installation + realm/project/environment/view/log + witnessEpoch + readKeyEpoch + policyEpoch + seq + envelopeHash. Same seq accepted only same hash.
reader.crashRecovery: if watermark persisted before target write, repeat same or newer canonical head only, recheck witness before writing. Never decrease watermark; pending old intent cannot bypass strict-current gate after restore.
reader.noOp: new envelope for same plaintext advances accepted checkpoint but leaves target data revision and rollout unchanged
reader.unavailable: preserve existing Secret per Retain availability policy, Ready/DataCurrent=false, no fresh application or new rollout; new target not created from cached stale data
reader.restore: fresh installation or lost/restored local state obtains current witness proof >= independent bootstrap checkpoint; StateMissing requires explicit restore/rebootstrap, never TOFU
reader.applicationBoundary: does not erase values already in app memory/env and cannot prevent an admin/etcd restore from exposing an older existing Kubernetes Secret before reconciliation. Strong startup freshness needs separate admission/app gate; not promised here.
reader.pendingRollout: E2E2 pending intent also needs successful strict-current reconciliation; new panel/witness failure freezes pending restarts. Ordinary Plain mode retains its separately specified behavior.
reader.stateAtomicity: checkpoint advances durably before target write; target write atomically records accepted seq/hash and eligible rollout intent. State/target mismatch is never inferred successful from labels; rerun strict verification or require admin recovery.

inheritance.model: full materialized views; immutable signed parent snapshot references, no server-side merging after signature
inheritance.propagation: parent update requires explicit child/view republish by authorized writer. UI shows DependencyPublicationRequired. Current canonical child is the last explicitly published materialization, not automatically latest parent.
inheritance.renames: realm/project/environment/view UUIDs remain stable across route renames. Renaming a field/path requires re-encryption and a new snapshot. Delete+recreate gets new UUID/log registration.
inheritance.folders: partial cryptographic access needs separate view+readKey; operator local selection is not secrecy boundary

lifecycle.migration: trusted client verifies explicit v1 source baseline, decrypts current approved values, creates new view key/publisher authority, signs initial e2e2 full view, commits to witness, installs independent trust bundle, then atomically switches mode. v1 history not authenticated retroactively.
lifecycle.legacy: existing e2e1 projects/agents keep old explicit mode; e2e2 readers reject e2e1/plaintext. Old agents receive UpgradeRequired for e2e2, never downgraded values.
lifecycle.writerRotation: independent authority authorizes new signing policy, stages new-signed snapshot+reader wrappers, atomically activates policy+head at witness, updates trust bundle. Old key cannot sign future canonical commits.
lifecycle.readRotation: new independent view read key, epoch+1, full new ciphertext, new wrappers for retained readers; commit new sequence; no header-only epoch bump.
lifecycle.recovery: no panel-initiated epoch/reset. Unrecoverable history requires explicit independently authorized new log/trust epoch, audited migration, consumers stopped until new trust installed.

implementationImpact: new witness module/service and durable external ledger adapter
stable realm/project/environment/view/log UUIDs; immutable envelopes and staged/committed state
new full-snapshot APIs and typed errors; legacy per-key write/approve/import/copy/rename/restore refused for e2e2
trusted writer distribution and separate read/publish key bundles
SDK new e2e2 codec, signature and witness verifier; legacy e2e1 isolated
operator strict current-head gate, durable checkpoint and E2E2 trust schema
migration and independent security review required before production release
referenceCoverage: design reference model fixes read-key and publisher policy epoch=1; Go codec/wrapper/witness/reader are now implemented and tested separately. No proof of actual rotation workflow, revoked-signer ledger restore, ledger durability, real panel transport or production security audit

stage3.implementation: operator/internal/e2e2, internal/witness/PinnedVerifier, internal/verification/Reader and independent bootstrap decoder
stage3.trustKeys: independently pinned Ed25519 keys must be canonical nonidentity prime-subgroup points; maintained edwards25519 group library checks points, standard crypto/ed25519 signs/verifies
stage3.freshness: Reader creates fresh CSPRNG nonces internally, verifies exact floor=max(bootstrap, trusted local checkpoint), exact canonical hash/full snapshot/wrap, then a second independent proof. Up to3 attempts; highest observed verified floor is retained during retries. No caller-provided head is accepted as current without signed proof.
stage3.stateBoundary: local checkpoint input must already be bound to installationID/bootstrapGeneration/trust identity by the state adapter. nil denotes an explicitly authorized new bootstrap; lost or replaced state must never silently become nil. Persistence and target writes remain stage4.
stage3.publisherBoundary: SealSnapshot and WrapReader are explicit in-process cryptographic building blocks, not a trusted writer UI, approval service, network staging client or witness commit workflow. They do not fetch unsigned source data or automatically rebase/sign.
stage3.interop: Node24 built-in HKDF has a1024-byte info limit. Independent test reference implements exact RFC5869 via WebCrypto HMAC and verifies long JCS header info including16 parents against Python/Go; wire/KDF inputs unchanged. This is not a production JS or browser UI claim.
stage3.integrationGate: controller retains its stage2 fail-closed behavior and RBAC; no live source fetch, target Secret mutation, checkpoint persistence or rollout is enabled by stage3
stage3.noZeroizationClaim: temporary mutable key buffers are cleared where practical; immutable strings, runtime copies and garbage collection prevent a guaranteed complete memory erasure claim
